subject: BlueHarbor model distribution & mirror access — scope and commercial terms
messages:
From: Alex Nguyen <alex@blueharbormodels.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@blueharbormodels.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Distribution partnership proposal — BlueHarbor models

Sergio,

Great to meet at the Infra+ML summit last week — appreciate the time. BlueHarbor would like to propose a distribution partnership: we’d grant Redwood permission to host and redistribute our new LlamaX-14B/quant weights under a limited distribution license so you can offer the model through Hosted and Dedicated modes.

High level ask:
- Mirror-hosting permission for Redwood (your hosted & dedicated infra) with read-only artifact access.
- Commercial fee: revenue share or flat licensing — open to Redwood’s preference.
- Branding + attribution guidelines included.

I attached a first-pass term sheet (BH_Distro_Terms_v1.pdf). We’re aiming for a pragmatic agreement that preserves our attribution and export controls while making it easy for partners to serve the model at scale. Ellen (cc) is our counsel and will handle redlines.

Can you confirm Redwood’s typical requirements about key management for mirrored weights, access auditing, and whether you need a mirror-only repo or the ability to create model variants (quantized / fine-tuned)?

Best,
Alex Nguyen
Head of Partnerships | BlueHarbor Models
https://blueharbormodels.com

[attachment: BH_Distro_Terms_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@blueharbormodels.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Distribution partnership proposal — BlueHarbor models

Alex — thanks for the note and the term sheet. Quick answers up front: yes, Redwood can host a mirror repo and serve weights through Hosted and Dedicated. We have production controls you’ll want in the agreement:

- KMS integration: support for customer-managed keys in Private deployments; for Hosted we keep keys and can support HSM-backed custody.
- Audit logs: token-level request logs and artifact-access audit trails are available and we can provide export snapshots for audits.
- Model variant policy: we typically allow quantization and optimizations for inference performance, but derivatives (public re-distribution or training-publish) require explicit rights.

Marissa (cc) will start a short internal assessment and map commercial options (rev-share vs licensing). Laura can cover legal/contract templates.

We’ll review the attached term sheet and propose specific redlines for licensing language around mirror access, watermarking/attribution, and embargo windows.

Two quick questions for you: 1) Do you require token-level watermarking for outputs? 2) Any export control or restricted-countries list we should be aware of?

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

[inline: downloaded BH_Distro_Terms_v1.pdf]

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@blueharbormodels.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Nguyen <alex@blueharbormodels.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Distribution partnership proposal — BlueHarbor models

Sergio / Marissa — thanks for the quick reply. A few legal clarifications from our side:

- Watermarking: not required as a hard term, but BlueHarbor prefers metadata tagging (non-public) and clear attribution when the model is served commercially.
- Derivatives: permission to quantize for inference is fine; fine-tuning that results in new public releases requires approval and revenue-sharing.
- Export controls: we cannot permit distribution into embargoed countries per our internal policy — we will provide a list.
- Vulnerability disclosure: we need a defined cadence for patching and a channel for security advisories.

We attached an editable term-sheet and would like Redwood’s redlines on Sections 3 (License scope), 5 (Security & audit), and 8 (Commercial terms).

Ellen Park
General Counsel, BlueHarbor Models

[attachment: BH_Distro_Terms_v1.pdf (redlines)]

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@blueharbormodels.com>, ellen.park@blueharbormodels.com
Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Distribution partnership proposal — BlueHarbor models

Alex / Ellen — reviewing here. Summary of Redwood’s proposed updates (high level):

- License scope: Mirror-hosting + serving allowed for Hosted & Dedicated customers. Private deployments are allowed but only under a separate enterprise addendum.
- Derivative works: quantization & inference-optimizations allowed; fine-tuning allowed for Redwood-managed fine-tunes with a share of revenue (suggest 20% revenue share on fine-tuned model licensing). Public redistribution of fine-tuned checkpoints prohibited.
- Audit and security: Redwood will provide weekly artifact-access exports for the first 90 days, then monthly; SOC 2 report can be shared under NDA. We require a 30-day SLA for critical security notices.
- Commercial: propose a blended rev-share for hosted usage (12%) or a fixed license fee for Dedicated mirror instances (TBD by capacity).
- Attribution: we will include BlueHarbor attribution in model metadata and UI banners; we prefer not to force watermarking.

Attached is a short spreadsheet with mirror requirements (redwood_mirror_requirements.xlsx) and our commercial scenarios. Can you confirm which commercial model you prefer so we can draft a single-sheet MSA?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call this week.

—Marissa
Head of GTM Partnerships, Redwood Inference

[attachment: redwood_mirror_requirements.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Alex Nguyen <alex@blueharbormodels.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@blueharbormodels.com>
Date: 2026-10-16T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Distribution partnership proposal — BlueHarbor models

Marissa / Sergio — this is helpful, thanks. BlueHarbor prefers the revenue-share model for Hosted (we like the 12% blended number) and a fixed annual license for Dedicated mirrors (we’ll propose numbers after we see usage buckets). A few follow-ups:

- Can Redwood commit to not exposing raw checkpoint download links to end customers? We’re okay with server-side mirror access for serving, but raw checkpoint exports must be restricted.
- For fine-tuning revenue share: BlueHarbor accepts the 20% split if Redwood agrees to co-market and include BlueHarbor in product listing metadata.
- Ellen will produce a revised term-sheet with the commercial options and a preliminary export-control list early next week.

We should be able to get to a signature-ready MSA by the end of October if both sides move quickly — would you like us to send a DocuSign link with the rev-share option pre-selected?

Cheers,
Alex
Head of Partnerships | BlueHarbor Models

[inline: noted — will review and schedule legal sync]
